mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz AMG GT R engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement M178 LS2 engine for a GT R typically costs between £5,500 and £19,000 depending on condition. Used units start from £5,500-£9,000, reconditioned from £11,000-£15,000, and fully rebuilt from £11,000-£19,000. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,500 for AMG-specialist work. A typical GT R is worth £100,000-£195,000, making engine replacement a viable investment for well-maintained cars.

mainEntity.name: Does the AMG GT R have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The GT R uses the M178 LS2 engine, which has a timing chain, not a belt. However, the M178 is known for timing chain stretch - a rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign. An NHTSA Technical Service Bulletin (LI05.10-P-049909) identifies timing chain stretch as a known issue, noting that vehicles with less than 50,000 kilometres require individual assessment.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of engine problems in an AMG GT R?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs of engine problems in the GT R include: a rattling noise on cold start (timing chain stretch), loss of power or limp mode (turbo actuator failure), white steam from the engine bay or low coolant warnings (crossover pipe leak), and blue smoke on startup or after overrun (valve stem seal failure). Owners also report stuck injectors, oil leaks from the transmission case, and faulty exhaust flaps as known issues.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an AMG GT R?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the car's condition and mileage. A GT R is typically worth £100,000-£195,000 - a rebuilt M178 LS2 engine (£11,000-£19,000) is usually well within the car's value and can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. For lower-value examples or those with multiple issues, a specialist repair may be more economical than a full replacement.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the M178 LS2 in the GT R and the M178 in other AMG GT models?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M178 LS2 in the GT R produces 577-585 hp - significantly more than the base GT (462 hp) and GT S (510 hp). It features upgraded turbos with larger compressor wheels, increased boost pressure (1.35 bar vs 1.2 bar), revised camshafts and exhaust manifolds, and larger intercoolers. The GT R also uses a dry-sump oiling system and is hand-built under AMG's 'One Man, One Engine' philosophy.

mainEntity.name: What causes the AMG GT R to lose power?

acceptedAnswer.text: Power loss in the GT R is most commonly caused by turbo actuator failure, which sends the car into limp mode. An NHTSA document identifies intermittent reduced power (no boost reading) as a known issue, recommending checks of wastegate linkage, pressure transducer, and vacuum supply. Other causes include boost leaks, timing chain stretch, and carbon buildup on intake valves.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz AMG GT R - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The AMG GT R arrived in 2016 as the track-focused flagship of the C190 AMG GT range, positioned above the GT S and GT C. Powered by the M178 LS2 - a hand-built 4.0-litre V8 biturbo producing 585 hp - the GT R was developed with input from AMG's GT3 racing programme, featuring a wider track, rear-wheel steering, and a "Green Hell Magno" launch colour that paid homage to its Nürburgring development. Only 750 GT R Pro units were produced globally, with approximately 80 allocated to the UK .

milestones.description: M178 LS2, 4.0L V8 biturbo, 577 hp (430 kW) - GT R launch at Goodwood Festival of Speed; 700 Nm torque; 0-62 mph in 3.6 seconds; top speed 198 mph
Production ramps up; GT R becomes available in "Green Hell Magno" as signature colour
GT R Pro launched with aerodynamics and chassis upgrades; same M178 LS2 engine; limited to 750 units globally
GT R Roadster introduced; limited-run open-top version with same powertrain
C190 production ends; GT R discontinued

commonProblems.h3: The M178 LS2 in the GT R is a masterpiece of performance engineering, delivering 585 hp from a hand-built 4.0-litre V8 . However, even AMG's finest have known weak points. Timing chain stretch, turbo actuator failure, and coolant crossover pipe leaks dominate replacement demand. problems.h4: M178 LS2 Timing Chain Stretch - Why the GT R Rattles on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The timing chain can stretch over time, particularly on cars with frequent track use or aggressive driving . An NHTSA Technical Service Bulletin (LI05.10-P-049909) identifies timing chain stretch as a known issue on M178 engines, noting that vehicles with less than 50,000 kilometres (31,068 miles) require individual assessment . Symptoms include a rattling or slapping noise from the engine, especially during startup , power loss, and rough idling .

repairOptions.longevity: Best done at first rattle; prevents catastrophic failure

problems.group: M178 LS2 Turbocharger Actuator & Bearing Failure
problems.h4: M178 LS2 Turbocharger Actuator & Bearing Failure - Boost Loss and Limp Mode
problems.rootCause: The hot-vee turbo placement exposes actuator electronics to extreme heat cycles, causing internal circuit board failure. The GT R's higher boost pressure (1.35 bar vs 1.2 bar in base GT) can accelerate turbo bearing wear. An NHTSA document identifies intermittent reduced power (no boost reading) as a known issue, recommending checks of wastegate linkage, pressure transducer, and vacuum supply .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace electronic boost actuator only, recalibrate
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before wastegate damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove turbos, replace bearings, wastegates, actuators
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for cars with worn but not seized turbos

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - rebuilt engine with upgraded turbos
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with reinforced turbo seals and upgraded actuators
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended when both turbos have failed

problems.recommendation: Turbo actuator failure is often misdiagnosed as a boost leak or vacuum issue. Get a diagnostic scan first - check wastegate linkage operation and pressure transducer actuation via XENTRY . If only the actuator has failed, replacement is cost-effective. If wastegate bushings are also worn or turbos have oil seal leaks, a full turbo rebuild is the sensible middle ground. For high-mileage cars (80k+), investing in a rebuilt engine with upgraded turbo components protects your GT R for years.

problems.group: M178 LS2 Hot-Vee Coolant Crossover Pipe Leak
problems.h4: M178 LS2 Hot-Vee Coolant Crossover Pipe Leak - The #1 Cooling System Failure
problems.rootCause: The plastic coolant crossover pipe mounted between the cylinder banks in the hot-vee degrades from sustained heat exposure. Once cracked, coolant leaks directly onto the hot turbo housings - creating steam, triggering low coolant warnings, and eventually causing overheating. The GT R's higher boost and track usage accelerate this failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace plastic pipe with OEM or upgraded aluminium unit, refill coolant
repairOptions.longevity: Permanent fix if upgraded aluminium pipe used

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace crossover pipe, both intercooler bricks, coolant hoses
repairOptions.longevity: For cars with chronic coolant loss or evidence of overheating

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with upgraded cooling system components

problems.recommendation: This is the most common coolant-related failure on M178 engines. Do not ignore low coolant warnings - driving with a cracked crossover pipe leads to rapid overheating and catastrophic engine damage. Replace the plastic pipe with an aftermarket aluminium unit as a preventative measure on any GT R over 40,000 miles. If caught early, the pipe replacement alone solves the problem for good.
